story.title: U.S. Envoys Visit Moscow to Revive Peace Talks Amid Ceasefire
story.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to renew efforts to end the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. During their visit, both Ukraine and Russia announced a three-day ceasefire, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urging a halt to airstrikes. The envoys are expected to meet with Russian officials before traveling to Kyiv for further discussions.

event_overview.title: About Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.subject: Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.summary: The Gaza Peace Deal refers to the second-phase roadmap announced in late July 2026 for implementing President Trump’s broader Gaza peace framework. It links the decommissioning of Hamas and other armed groups’ weapons, a transition to Palestinian civilian administration, deployment of an international stabilization force, phased Israeli withdrawal, and Gaza’s reconstruction; implementation depends on agreed sequencing and verification.

facts.label: Announcement and framework
facts.value: The roadmap was made public on July 31, 2026, as “A Roadmap for Completing the Implementation of President Trump’s Comprehensive Peace Plan in Gaza,” and identifies the Comprehensive Plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025) as its international framework.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The plan concerns the Gaza Strip, with provisions addressing its governance, internal security, humanitarian assistance, reconstruction, armed groups, and the withdrawal of Israeli forces.

facts.label: Governance transition
facts.value: The roadmap calls for civilian governance and security functions to pass to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), while Resolution 2803 establishes the Board of Peace as the transitional body to coordinate the framework and redevelopment of Gaza.

facts.label: Security force and Israeli withdrawal
facts.value: A temporary International Stabilization Force is envisaged to monitor the ceasefire, support aid delivery, train Palestinian police, and support the transition. Israeli withdrawal is phased and linked to the disarmament process and an agreed timetable; Resolution 2803 authorizes the Board of Peace and related international presences through December 31, 2027, unless the Security Council acts further.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of late-July to mid-August 2026 developments concerning the roadmap’s announcement, responses, and related regional military tensions; it does not constitute a complete record of the Gaza war, prior ceasefire diplomacy, or all implementation activity.

explore_lenses.label: Is this a full ceasefire across Ukraine?
explore_lenses.title: A limited air-strike pause, not a nationwide truce
explore_lenses.summary: The announced restraint is tied to the envoys’ travel and talks, and its stated scope is narrower than a general ceasefire ending combat across Ukraine. Reported strikes immediately before the pause underline that fighting has not otherwise stopped.

claims.text: The Kremlin said Putin ordered no strikes against Kyiv for 72 hours beginning at midnight on September 5; the reported order is specifically framed around the capital, not all Ukrainian territory or all military operations.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine would refrain from air strikes needed to enable the U.S. visit and called on Russia to reciprocate; he described this as protection for the negotiators rather than a concession to Russia.

Before the announced pause took effect, Ukrainian officials reported Russian overnight strikes on Kamianske and further strikes near Kyiv and Boryspil, so the available reporting does not establish a broader halt in hostilities.

explore_lenses.label: What still divides Moscow and Kyiv?
explore_lenses.title: Territory and security guarantees remain central
explore_lenses.summary: The trip resumes diplomacy after a pause, but publicly available accounts show that the parties still differ on territorial control and Ukraine’s future security arrangements. The U.S. has not released the text of its current proposal.

claims.text: A Reuters report said the Kremlin’s position includes Ukraine ceding the full territory of four regions claimed by Russia and abandoning its NATO ambition; Ukraine rejects territorial surrender as unacceptable.

In a November 2025 White House readout of talks with Ukraine, the Ukrainian delegation said the draft under discussion addressed security guarantees, sovereignty, infrastructure protection, freedom of navigation and economic development—issues that indicate the breadth of a prospective settlement beyond a battlefield pause.

Zelenskyy said Kyiv would assess both what Witkoff and Kushner bring and Moscow’s response, emphasizing that Ukraine is seeking “real options” to move the war toward an end rather than announcing agreement with a plan.

story_report.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are in Moscow in a renewed push for talks to end the war in Ukraine, with a planned follow-on visit to Kyiv. The visit has prompted limited temporary restraint: the Kremlin said Vladimir Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight Sept. 5, while President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would refrain from air strikes to protect the negotiators and called on Russia to reciprocate. No agreement has been announced.

sections.heading: Ceasefire Scope Remains Limited
sections.body: The announced three-day pause does not establish a general ceasefire across Ukraine. The Kremlin’s reported order was framed as a halt to strikes on Kyiv, rather than all Ukrainian territory or all military activity. Before the pause took effect, Ukrainian officials reported Russian overnight attacks on Kamianske and further strikes near Kyiv and Boryspil, leaving the broader state of hostilities unchanged in the available reporting.

sections.heading: Territory and Security Divide Negotiators
sections.body: The prospective negotiations face disputes extending well beyond a temporary air-strike pause. Reuters reported that Moscow’s position includes Ukraine ceding the full territory of four regions claimed by Russia and giving up its NATO ambition, while Ukraine rejects territorial surrender as unacceptable. A previous White House account of talks with Ukraine said a draft addressed security guarantees, sovereignty, infrastructure protection, navigation freedom and economic development; Zelenskyy said Kyiv would evaluate both the envoys’ proposals and Moscow’s response for “real options” to end the war.

unresolved.text: Neither side has publicly detailed whether the temporary restraint covers drones, missiles, ground operations or targets beyond Kyiv, or how compliance would be verified.
The current U.S. proposal, Moscow’s response and any agreed language on territory or security guarantees have not been publicly released.
No public readout confirms whom the envoys will meet in Moscow, whether direct follow-on negotiations will occur, or whether the restraint will continue after the visit.
